value: This interview features Simon Johnson, economist and co-author of *Power and Progress: Our Thousand-Year Struggle Over Technology and Prosperity*. Johnson discusses the book's central argument that widespread prosperity from technological progress is not an automatic outcome but rather requires conscious efforts to steer its benefits beyond the elite. He illustrates this with historical examples from the Industrial Revolution and Middle Ages, and contemporary issues like AI and "so-so" automation that displaces workers without broadly boosting productivity. The conversation also explores pressing financial topics such as the implications of recent bank failures, the future of deposit insurance, and central bank digital currencies, alongside broader discussions on IMF reform, the role of institutions in economic growth, and effective US science policy.
